questions.question: According to PostgreSQL 17 Chapter 5, what does the chapter explain how to create in order to hold data?
questions.expected_answer: Database structures that hold data, primarily tables.
questions.evidence_quote: This chapter covers how one creates the database structures that will hold one's data.

questions.question: When a new row omits values for some columns, what happens to those columns?
questions.expected_answer: They are filled with their respective default values.
questions.evidence_quote: When a new row is created and no values are specified for some of the columns, those columns will be filled with their respective default values.

questions.question: How does an identity column generate key values?
questions.expected_answer: It is generated automatically from an implicit sequence.
questions.evidence_quote: An identity column is a special column that is generated automatically from an implicit sequence. It can be used to generate key values.

questions.question: What data is a generated column computed from?
questions.expected_answer: It is always computed from other columns.
questions.evidence_quote: A generated column is a special column that is always computed from other columns.

questions.question: What kind of condition can a CHECK constraint impose on a column value?
questions.expected_answer: The value must satisfy a Boolean expression.
questions.evidence_quote: It allows you to specify that the value in a certain column must satisfy a Boolean (truth-value) expression.

questions.question: When a primary key is added, what index is created and what additional condition is imposed on the key columns?
questions.expected_answer: A unique B-tree index is created and the key columns are marked NOT NULL.
questions.evidence_quote: Adding a primary key will automatically create a unique B-tree index on the column or group of columns listed in the primary key, and will force the column(s) to be marked NOT NULL.

questions.question: How can a foreign key reference a group of columns?
questions.expected_answer: Write it as a table constraint specifying the referencing and referenced column groups.
questions.evidence_quote: A foreign key can also constrain and reference a group of columns. As usual, it then needs to be written in table constraint form.

questions.question: In the Chapter 5 example, which foreign-key clause cascades a tenant deletion to referencing rows?
questions.expected_answer: Use ON DELETE CASCADE.
questions.evidence_quote: tenant_id integer REFERENCES tenants ON DELETE CASCADE

questions.question: When adding a column without specifying DEFAULT, what initial value is used?
questions.expected_answer: NULL.
questions.evidence_quote: The new column is initially filled with whatever default value is given (null if you don't specify a DEFAULT clause).

questions.question: When a column is removed, what happens to its data and the table constraints involving it?
questions.expected_answer: The column's data disappears and constraints involving it are dropped.
questions.evidence_quote: Whatever data was in the column disappears. Table constraints involving the column are dropped, too.

questions.question: Does ALTER COLUMN ... SET DEFAULT change existing rows or only affect future INSERT commands?
questions.expected_answer: It does not affect existing rows; it changes the default for future INSERT commands.
questions.evidence_quote: Note that this doesn't affect any existing rows in the table, it just changes the default for future INSERT commands.

questions.question: Which SQL statement shown grants SELECT on mytable to PUBLIC?
questions.expected_answer: GRANT SELECT ON mytable TO PUBLIC;
questions.evidence_quote: GRANT SELECT ON mytable TO PUBLIC;

questions.question: Besides tables, what named objects can a PostgreSQL schema contain?
questions.expected_answer: It can contain data types, functions, and operators, among other named objects.
questions.evidence_quote: Schemas also contain other kinds of named objects, including data types, functions, and operators.

questions.question: According to Chapter 7, how does the FROM clause derive the table used as query input?
questions.expected_answer: From one or more table references in a comma-separated list.
questions.evidence_quote: The FROM clause derives a table from one or more other tables given in a comma-separated table reference list.

questions.question: Which rows does GROUP BY combine into the same group?
questions.expected_answer: Rows with the same values in all listed columns.
questions.evidence_quote: The GROUP BY clause is used to group together those rows in a table that have the same values in all the columns listed.

questions.question: According to Chapter 5, what does the manual recommend for most columns in typical database designs?
questions.expected_answer: Mark most columns NOT NULL.
questions.evidence_quote: In most database designs the majority of columns should be marked not null.

questions.question: According to Chapter 5, what does the TRIGGER privilege allow?
questions.expected_answer: It allows creation of a trigger on a table, view, or other listed relation.
questions.evidence_quote: TRIGGER Allows creation of a trigger on a table, view, etc.

questions.question: According to Chapter 5, if pg_catalog is not named explicitly in the search path, when is it searched?
questions.expected_answer: It is implicitly searched before the schemas named in the path.
questions.evidence_quote: If it is not named explicitly in the path then it is implicitly searched before searching the path's schemas.

questions.question: In Chapter 7, what result shape does the documented three-row VALUES example return?
questions.expected_answer: A table with two columns and three rows.
questions.evidence_quote: will return a table of two columns and three rows.

questions.question: According to Chapter 7, are recursive WITH queries evaluated recursively or iteratively internally?
questions.expected_answer: They are evaluated iteratively internally.
questions.evidence_quote: internally such queries are evaluated iteratively.
